title: The Third Declension — i-Stems
subtitle: civis, mare, animal. Genitive plural -ium.
objectives: Decline third-declension i-stem nouns in all cases.
Recognize i-stem nouns by their genitive plural -ium.

sections.heading: The third declension: i-stems
sections.body:
Some third-declension nouns have an -i- that appears in certain forms. The main marker is the genitive plural: -ium instead of -um.

Paradigm: civis, civis (citizen, m./f.):

          Singular    Plural
  Nom.    civis       civēs
  Gen.    civis       civium
  Dat.    civī        civibus
  Acc.    civem       civēs (or civīs)
  Abl.    cive        civibus

Neuter i-stems have -e nominative/accusative singular and -ia plural:
  mare, maris (sea) → nominative/accusative plural: maria
  animal, animālis (animal) → nominative/accusative plural: animālia

Cicero writes: cīvēs Rōmānī. — Roman citizens.
